A rig built from your own nodes

1. Your loaders go into Rig Model. Wire its model into your sampler. The Workspace adds this rig's LoRAs and camera LoRAs to it for you.
2. Rig Inputs hands your sampler the prompts, latent, seed, steps, CFG, sampler, scheduler and denoise from the Workspace.
3. Your sampler's latent goes into Rig Result.

On the Workspace, the Models tab has a rig named My rig of kind Your own nodes. Type your prompt on the Prompts tab and queue. There are no wires to the Workspace: the three rig nodes find it by the rig name. Swap the KSampler for any sampler you like.

nodes.title: RedNode Studio 1.4
widgets_values:
# RedNode Studio 1.4

Open **RedNode Start Here Install** from the template browser first and let ComfyUI Manager
install what it offers. It holds one node from each pack this workflow can use, so Manager
finds them in one pass instead of one at a time. Restart ComfyUI, then open this workflow.

Without that step the graph opens with missing nodes in red.

## Node packs this workflow needs

| Pack | What it does here |
| --- | --- |
| [RedNode Studio](https://github.com/RedNodeAI/ComfyUI-RedNodeStudio) | The Workspace, the rigs, the prompt tools, the notes |
| [ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF) | The GGUF text encoder loader on the ZTurbo rig |
| [Krea2-BBOX-Prompter](https://github.com/ukr8b3g-cmyk/Krea2-BBOX-Prompter) | The Light & Color and Scene nodes |
| [ComfyUI-Krea-Moodboards](https://github.com/Andro-Meta/ComfyUI-Krea-Moodboards) | The Style browser |
| [ComfyUI-EulerDiscreteScheduler](https://github.com/erosDiffusion/ComfyUI-EulerDiscreteScheduler) | The FlowMatch scheduler on the ZTurbo rig |
| [Derfuu_ComfyUI_ModdedNodes](https://github.com/Derfuu/Derfuu_ComfyUI_ModdedNodes) | The text node feeding the prompt |

Optional, and only if you switch them on inside the Workspace: the caption engines, the
Detailer's upscalers and segmenter, and the Post tab's depth and mask models. The Overview
tab's **Check installs** button tells you which of those your own settings call for, and
links to each. Nothing there is needed to render.

## Model files

Put each file in the folder named, then pick it on the Models tab.

**Diffusion models** into `models/diffusion_models`

| File | Used by | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `krea2TurboOfficialComfy_krea2TurboFp8.safetensors` | the Krea2Raw rig | [Krea 2 Turbo Official Comfy-Org Checkpoints](https://civitai.com/models/2726029/krea-2-turbo-official-comfy-org-checkpoints-krea2), the fp8 file |
| `darkBeast_darkblitz6Beyondnsfw.safetensors` | the ZTurbo rig | [on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/justabigduck/my_saves/blob/58f4f01caf3204ad067d3841b51cf4f8e2d5aecb/realistic_models/darkBeast_darkblitz6Beyondnsfw.safetensors) |
| `pornmasterKrea2_v2TurboInt8.safetensors` | the Krea2 rig | [on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Lucas77077/Krea-2-Models/blob/main/pornmasterKrea2_v2TurboInt8.safetensors) |

The Krea2 rig's file is an INT8 build. If it will not load, set that rig's **Loader** on the
Models tab to **INT8 W8A8** and install ComfyUI-INT8-Fast, which the Start here workflow
offers. An INT8 file looks like any other `.safetensors`, so the loader cannot tell from the
name alone.

**Text encoders** into `models/text_encoders`

| File | Used by | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qwen3VLInstruct4bHeretic_v10.safetensors` | Krea 2 rigs, CLIP type `krea2` | [Qwen3-VL-4b-Heretic for ComfyUI](https://huggingface.co/DreamFast/Qwen3-VL-4b-Heretic-ComfyUI). Any build in there works; pick one your card fits |
| `Qwen3-4B-abliterated_dark.safetensors` | the ZTurbo rig, CLIP type `lumina2` | [Huihui Qwen3-4B-abliterated for ComfyUI](https://huggingface.co/AEmotionStudio/Huihui-Qwen3-4B-abliterated-v2-CLIP), from [huihui-ai/Qwen3-4B-abliterated](https://huggingface.co/huihui-ai/Qwen3-4B-abliterated) |

**VAEs** into `models/vae`

| File | Used by | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wan_2.1_vae_fp32.safetensors` | Krea 2 rigs | [Comfy-Org Wan 2.1 VAE](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Wan_2.1_ComfyUI_repackaged/tree/main/split_files/vae). That one is the standard build; this workflow uses an fp32 conversion of it |
| `UltraFlux.safetensors` | the ZTurbo rig | [UltraFlux VAE](https://civitai.com/models/2231253/ultraflux-vae-or-improved-quality-for-flux-and-zimage) |

## LoRA files

Put each file in `models/loras`. The Workspace's **LoRA** tab lists all three, switched on
at strength 1.00, and a row turns red when its file is not found. Switch a row off if you
would rather not load it; only the Identity edit has a mode that depends on it.

| File | What it does | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `krea2_identity_edit_v1_2.safetensors` | The Krea 2 Identity edit. Keeps the face and body of your reference through a re-render, a swap or a restage, and the Identity mode on the Img2Img tab needs it in the stack | [Krea 2 Identity Edit](https://civitai.com/models/2761113/krea-2-identity-edit) v1.2, by lbouaraba. Also on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/conradlocke/krea2-identity-edit), where the r128 build is half the size and close to it |
| `Krea2_TextFusion_Refusal_Reduction.safetensors` | Loosens the refusal the base model learned in its text conditioning, so prompts it already understands stop coming out generic. Adds no look of its own | [Krea2 TextFusion Refusal-Reduction LoRA](https://civitai.com/models/2775340/krea2-textfusion-refusal-reduction-lora) v1.0, which is the file named here. Also on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Quiho/Krea2_TextFusion_Refusal-Reduction_LoRA_v1.0_lora) |
| `krea2filterbypass3.safetensors` | Turns off the safety filter built into the model, which otherwise steers a flagged prompt toward a censored picture | [Krea2 Filter Bypass](https://civitai.com/models/2746817/krea2-filter-bypass-fedor) by Fedor. Also on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/uzumix/krea2filterbypass3.safetensors) |

## The rigs

Three rigs live on the Models tab. One is active at a time and renders; a prompt can name
another by rig name.

- **Krea2**: loads its files on the Models tab. 8 steps, cfg 1, euler_ancestral / simple.
- **Krea2Raw**: Your own nodes, running through the `krea2_external` chain on the canvas.
Marked as the official Krea 2 Turbo, which is what the identity edit wants.
- **ZTurbo**: Your own nodes, running through the `ZTurbo` chain. 12 steps, cfg 1
euler / simple, with the FlowMatch scheduler and a split sigma pair.

A rig set to **Your own nodes** is driven by the **Built-in sampler**. That sounds backwards
and it is worth reading twice: your own sampler does the work, and the Workspace hands it the
prompts, the latent, the seed and the numbers through Rig Inputs, then takes the picture back
from Rig Result. On **External sampler** the Workspace renders nothing at all and those rigs
never run.

The `rig3` chain, in the group marked PLUG YOUR OWN RIG HERE, is an empty slot for your own
sampler. Name a rig after it on the Models tab, set that rig to Your own nodes, and it runs.

## Using it

1. Pick the rig on the **Models** tab.
2. Write the prompt on the **Prompts** tab. A row can be tied to one rig by name.
3. Press **Generate** on the **Run** tab and watch the stages, the picture and the memory.
4. The **Overview** tab maps the whole run in the order it happens: green is on, grey is off
amber is on but stood aside, red wants fixing. Hover a box for the reason, click one to
open the page that decides it.

Nothing is saved unless **Save** is switched on, on the Run tab. The finished picture still
shows in the Live picture and the Review either way.

## VRAM

Set **VRAM limit** on the Run tab to your card. The line under it says what the run needs
with nothing held, and whether it will hold to stay under the limit. Holding is slower but
keeps a big rig inside a small card. On a card with room to spare, Free range is faster.
